title: What are the built-in Java annotations?
shortTitle: What are the built-in Java annotations?
keyPoints: @Override: compile-time check that the method actually overrides a parent method
@Deprecated: marks a method/class as outdated – compiler warns when used
@SuppressWarnings: tells the compiler to suppress specific warnings
@FunctionalInterface: ensures the interface has exactly one abstract method (for lambdas)
@SafeVarargs: suppresses heap pollution warnings for generic varargs

s1_definition.oneliner: @Override ensures correct overriding, @Deprecated marks outdated code, @SuppressWarnings silences warnings, @FunctionalInterface enforces single-abstract-method. Meta-annotations control annotation behavior.
s1_definition.profdef:
Built-in annotations fall into two groups:

- **Code annotations:** @Override, @Deprecated, @SuppressWarnings, @FunctionalInterface, @SafeVarargs.
- **Meta-annotations (annotations on annotations):** @Target (where it can be used), @Retention (how long it survives: SOURCE, CLASS, RUNTIME), @Documented, @Inherited, @Repeatable.
s1_definition.analogy: @Override is a stamp that says "this form replaces the head office version" – if it does not match, the stamp is rejected. @Deprecated is a "discontinued" label on an old banking product. @SuppressWarnings is the branch manager signing off on a known warning.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Java's built-in annotations provide compile-time safety and documentation. @Override catches overriding mistakes. @Deprecated marks outdated code. @FunctionalInterface enforces the lambda contract. Meta-annotations like @Target and @Retention control where and how long custom annotations survive.

One sentence to remember: @Override catches typos, @Deprecated warns users, @FunctionalInterface enforces one abstract method, and @Retention(RUNTIME) makes annotations readable by frameworks.
